Nothing here was captured live by the original deployment run. See docs/TRANCHE_2_DEPLOYMENT_EVIDENCE_CLOSURE.md for the full method and for every verification command, reproducible read-only.

usdy_sac.wasm_sha256: built-in (Stellar Asset Contract, not a Principal-source contract)
usdy_sac.verification: Recovered from the asset issuer account's (not the deployer's) own Horizon operation history, same 2 November 2026 practice session as the five upload transactions above. This transaction predates Soroban RPC's getTransaction retention window (status NOT_FOUND there), so verified two ways instead of via resultMetaXdr: (1) its envelope_xdr (from Horizon, which keeps full history regardless of RPC's retention window), decoded locally, shows the real operation is invoke_host_function.host_function.create_contract with executable == "stellar_asset" (the built-in Stellar Asset Contract, explicitly distinct from a create_contract with a custom wasm hash) and contract_id_preimage.asset.credit_alphanum4 == {asset_code: USDY, issuer: GDUGKHAJJPEYRF4T5XG7HJSUY3AGMHKHCSTSLZSGOCK2673N5ZKDFIDT}, matching exactly; (2) the resulting SAC address for that exact asset was independently, deterministically recomputed offline (`stellar contract id asset --asset USDY:GDUGKHAJJPEYRF4T5XG7HJSUY3AGMHKHCSTSLZSGOCK2673N5ZKDFIDT --network testnet`, a pure local computation from the network passphrase and the asset -- no chain call, no return-value metadata needed, since a Stellar Asset Contract's address is a deterministic function of its asset, not of anything the creating transaction returns) and the result matches this id exactly: CB2YO6BCOTN336RQUAMHOBCNABJG74URBIMNUHXB27K2QOLJKDCDXODZ.
usdy_sac.note: Created via the built-in Stellar Asset Contract path (create_contract with executable=stellar_asset), not a deploy_contract() wasm upload/deploy pair -- correctly excluded from the 12 CreateContract-with-wasm operations enumerated above, and verified by a different, asset-specific method rather than left unresolved.

source_to_byte_reproducibility.builder_machine: this verification's own machine, rustc 1.94.1 (e408947bf 2026-03-25), same command as the dApp's own (cargo build --workspace --release --target wasm32v1-none) against an isolated `git archive` of commit 665bb6760372d30307a1a035da24e51776f727e8
source_to_byte_reproducibility.result: 0 of 12 byte-identical to the deployed/manifest hashes
source_to_byte_reproducibility.diagnosis: Consistent with, not contradicting, the dApp evidence doc's own TRANCHE_2_EVIDENCE.md section 2.1 finding (their CI runner also got 0 of 12 against the same source) -- most of these wasm files embed the building machine's own absolute path (via the cargo registry path), and the dApp's own matching build used Rust 1.95.0, not this verification's 1.94.1. A controlled comparison supports the version difference as at least a contributing factor: an isolated rebuild of the SAME machine's toolchain (1.94.1) against the separate TR2 deployment's commit aae6cf8 (see ../deployment-manifest.json) DID reproduce 12 of 12 byte-identical, because that manifest's own build was also made with 1.94.1. On-chain code matching the manifest (above) is independently and separately confirmed; this reproducibility result does not change that.

source_to_byte_reproducibility_followup_.purpose: The attempt above narrowed, but did not settle, whether the Rust 1.94.1 vs 1.95.0 version difference was the (or a) remaining explanation for 0/12, on top of the already-documented absolute-path embedding. This follow-up installs 1.95.0 explicitly -- the version the dApp's own evidence doc says its matching build used -- and tests that one variable in isolation, exactly as the original attempt said it had not yet done.
source_to_byte_reproducibility_followup_.builder_machine: rustc 1.95.0 (59807616e 2026-04-14), installed via `rustup toolchain install 1.95.0 --target wasm32v1-none` without changing this machine's default toolchain (confirmed unchanged: `rustup show active-toolchain` still reports stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu as default after this work)
source_to_byte_reproducibility_followup_.build_command: cargo +1.95.0 build --workspace --release --target wasm32v1-none --locked, against the same isolated `git archive` of commit 665bb6760372d30307a1a035da24e51776f727e8 the original attempt used (committed Cargo.lock honored via --locked, not regenerated)
source_to_byte_reproducibility_followup_.result: 0 of 12 byte-identical to the deployed/manifest hashes -- the exact same result as with 1.94.1, so the Rust version alone is not the explanation
source_to_byte_reproducibility_followup_.diagnosis: TESTED, not hypothesized: `strings` on this 1.95.0 build's own principal_oracle_adapter.wasm shows the embedded cargo-registry source path `/home/mohamed/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/soroban-sdk-26.0.1/src/ledger.rs` (this machine's own home directory); `strings` on the actual deployed wasm (freshly re-fetched from Testnet via `stellar contract fetch`, read-only) shows `/Users/cedric/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-1949cf8c6b5b557f/soroban-sdk-26.0.1/src/ledger.rs` instead -- a macOS path under a different builder's home directory entirely, with a different absolute length and a different OS path style, baked directly into the wasm's own debug/panic-message strings regardless of which Rust version produced it. This is a demonstrated, directly observed cause, not an inference from elsewhere: two builds differing only in their filesystem location will not produce byte-identical wasm no matter which Rust version either used, because the absolute source path is part of the compiled output itself. The Rust-version hypothesis from the original attempt is accordingly superseded by this more direct, confirmed explanation -- it is not ruled out as also contributing (a true controlled single-variable test of version alone would require building on the identical machine/path with both 1.94.1 and 1.95.0, which this follow-up did not do, since the path difference already fully explains the mismatch on its own), but the path embedding alone is sufficient to explain 0/12 with no need to invoke the version difference at all.
source_to_byte_reproducibility_followup_.what_was_not_done: No attempt was made to force a match by passing a path-remapping build flag (e.g. --remap-path-prefix) not used in either the dApp's or TR2's own original build process -- this task's own instructions say not to modify source, dependencies, or build settings merely to obtain matching bytes, and reproducing the ORIGINAL, as-built process (not a modified one that happens to match) is what this attestation is about. No recorded deployed hash, source_commit, or built_at field was changed as a result of this finding.
source_to_byte_reproducibility_followup_.on_chain_wasm_hash_verification_unaffect: The separate, independent claim in on_chain_wasm_hash_verification above (deployed bytecode matches this manifest's own recorded wasmHashes, 12 of 12) is not affected by this result in either direction -- that is a claim about the manifest and the chain agreeing with each other, not about either of them matching a fresh local build from source.
